verdicts.correct: the visible difference is the difference the setting makes, and it is readable
verdicts.weak: on the right subject but ambiguous, undirected, or too faint to read at tooltip size
verdicts.wrong: the picture does not show what the setting does

method: Every animation was WATCHED: all stored frames rendered as a contact sheet and read against the setting's own description in spacr/settings.py.

The pixel metric was used only as a floor, never as a verdict. It cannot see a composition fault in either direction: cytoplasm scores 13.5% (13th highest of 94) and shows nothing, while crop_mode scores 1.8% and is one of the clearest.

The border family was measured from pixels with spacr.setting_animations.measure_border_object_removal, which reads the well edge off the drawn rule and compares two frames at the SAME zoom -- never frame 0, which is zoomed out, and never the generator's own touches flag.

animations.note: Shows a grey blob pulsing in brightness. No nucleus, pathogen or organelle appears in ANY frame, so nothing is ever subtracted. Cause found in the generator: _cytoplasm draws all three and then paints over them with painter.line(..., closed=True), whose fill_closed defaults to True.

Meant as one blob cross-fading into two spots (62x30 at x=180 -> 32x25 at x=150 and x=210). Because both products use the same multi-stroke Golgi glyph and sit 60 px apart, they overlap each other and the fading original; the 'after' state is one wide mush, not two objects. The split the setting performs is not visible.
The box grows and a neighbouring cell appears -- the documented consequence -- but the mask-crop versus box-crop contrast itself is never drawn, and it reads much like png_size.

The drawing is right, but settings.py documents this key as DEPRECEATED and says the Cellpose-SAM path calls model.eval with diameter=None. An animation showing a visible effect for a setting with no effect is misleading by context.
